summary: Require every material EKODI AI operational claim to be evidence-gated, scope-matched, fresh, independently verifiable, and protected by a deterministic final-response guard so model speech cannot be mistaken for actual system state.
approvalBasis: The EKODI Platform owner identified continuing hallucination risk, reviewed the proposed Evidence-First and anti-hallucination approach, and explicitly instructed EKODI to modify the platform accordingly on 2026-09-23.
runtimeEnforcement: ai-claim-integrity.js detects material operational success language and blocks unsupported final responses
ai-control-provider-router.js applies the deterministic claim gate to origin-preserving final synthesis
ai-control-core.js instructs final synthesis that collaborator text, memory and prior chat are assertions rather than current-state proof
config/ai-change-orchestration-policy.json binds claim integrity to orchestration reporting
config/ai-development-completion-policy.json requires scope-matched claim receipts and independent verification
AGENTS.override.md and ORCHESTRATOR_PRODUCTION_CONTRACT.md make the rule provider-neutral and ecosystem-wide
rollback: If the deterministic guard causes a material reporting regression, revert the runtime guard/router integration to the previous guarded release while retaining the constitutional rule, repair claim classification or evidence projection, run claim-integrity and orchestration tests, then re-promote through the guarded release pipeline. Never roll back to allowing memory or model assertions to prove current operational completion.
verification: Run claim-integrity validator/unit tests, constitution validation, orchestration tests, provider-router regression tests, repository checks, guarded deployment, and real production verification of both supported and unsupported completion claims.
